items.title: NABKISAN Lists India’s First WASH-Focused Social Bond, Raises ₹180 Crore
items.summary: NABKISAN Finance Limited, a subsidiary of the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), on 1st October 2026 listed India’s first Social Bond dedicated exclusively to the Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) sector on the National Stock Exchange (NSE), Mumbai.
key_facts: The Social Bond issue witnessed robust investor participation and was oversubscribed 1.8 times, enabling NABKISAN to raise ₹180 crore.
The five-year bond carries a coupon rate of 8.10%, matures in September 2031, and has been assigned the highest domestic credit ratings of CRISIL AAA (Stable) and CARE AAA (Stable).

The proceeds will be deployed to expand access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene solutions across rural and underserved communities, contributing to improved health, livelihoods and quality of life.

items.title: Shri Rajiv Gauba calls for a shift to Light-Touch, Risk-Proportionate regulation at the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave
items.summary: Shri Rajiv Gauba, Member, NITI Aayog in his address at the plenary session on “Regulatory Oversight in an Age of Disruption” at the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave, highlighted the need for regulatory frameworks to evolve alongside a rapidly changing geopolitical, technological and economic environment.
key_facts: He emphasised that the challenge before policymakers is not to choose between regulation and growth, but to develop regulations that manage risks while supporting innovation, competition and investment.
He also highlighted the growing complexity of modern business models, which increasingly span multiple sectors and technologies.

He noted that regulators must carefully assess whether new rules are warranted before intervening in new and rapidly evolving sectors and avoid attempting to prescribe solutions for every possible failure.

items.title: Haryana’s Sporting Achievements Take Centre Stage in 8th Edition of PM Mementos Auction
items.summary: This edition features seven mementos from Haryana, with sporting achievements forming a prominent part of the collection. Five items are sports-related, while others celebrate the state’s religious and cultural heritage. Open for public bidding, these mementos carry stories of achievement and perseverance.
key_facts: Celebrating Haryana’s Paralympic Champions Among the featured items is an arrow presented by Harwinder Singh, who became the first Indian to win a Paralympic gold medal in archery.
Two mementos are associated with Navdeep Singh, who won gold in the men’s F41 javelin throw event at the Paris 2024 Paralympics.
His cap and signed shirt offer members of the public an opportunity to own keepsakes connected to this sporting achievement.

items.title: As part of Special Gram Sabha on Gandhi Jayanti, Jal Arpan Observed in more than 1850 Gram Panchayats Across Rural India to Strengthen Community Ownership of Rural Water Supply Systems Under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0
items.summary: On the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti and Special Gram Sabhas held across States/UTs, more than 1,850 Gram Panchayats/villages observed Jal Arpan- a key reform under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0- that places rural drinking water systems in the hands of the communities.
key_facts: In a first, the Jal Arpan module also enabled generation of Har Ghar Jal Certificates in regional languages for eligible Gram Panchayats and villages.

Activities such as Jal Sankalp, Jal Bandhan, demonstrations on water quality testing using Field Test Kits (FTKs), awareness programmes and recognition of community contributors were organised in several villages.

items.title: India’s First 5.56 km Free‑Space Quantum Key Distribution Link Demonstrated
items.summary: QNu Labs, in collaboration with Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo‑informatics (BISAG‑N) and IIT Gandhinagar, has successfully demonstrated India’s first free‑space Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) link at a scale of 5.56 km.
key_facts: Using QNu Labs’ Pointing, Acquisition and Tracking system, the trial achieved a stable Quantum Bit Error Rate below 5% and generated secure keys at a rate of 230–260 bps.

About IIT Gandhinagar: Founded in 2008, the Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar (IITGN) is a leading institution focused on excellence in engineering, science, technology, humanities and social sciences.
About QNu Labs: Founded in 2016, QNu Labs is India’s pioneer in quantum‑secure digital infrastructure, offering sovereign products and solutions deployed globally.
